text:
nick: quick heads-up  Marta got an H-1B transfer filed but counsel flagged the need for consular processing in a third country. proposed onsite start 2026-07-01 might slip. can people-ops advise on sign-on, relocation, and equity cliff if start moves?
marta: hey all 60a i'm currently in the UK and could travel for stamping but appointment waits might be long. i prefer to avoid losing signing bonus if start delayed.
ashley: short: payroll requires I-9 completion with US work auth; if stamping needed abroad and you can't start payroll by 7/1, payroll is delayed. sign-on and relocation payouts typically run through payroll, so they would slip unless we approve an exception.
kevin: from counsel: third-country stamping adds variability. once transfer receipt and consulate appointment are booked, timeline may be 4-12 weeks. we can sometimes request premium processing for adjudication but stamping speed depends on consulate availability.
nick: any flexibility on paying portion of sign-on early as an advance? finance/comp implications?
comp-bot: Note: sign-on bonus is taxable income and must be processed through payroll. Exception: we can issue a taxable lump-sum advance; requires signed advance agreement and tax withholding. Finance approval needed.
marta: would an advance affect equity vesting or PTO accrual?
ashley: equity and PTO anchor to payroll hire date by default. an advance payment does not change hire_date for vesting. we can escalate to comp for discretionary remedies but not guaranteed.
kevin: also flag travel risk: if Marta travels for stamping and a refusal occurs, that could delay further. counsel recommends waiting for a confirmed appointment and sharing the itinerary so we can advise.
nick: team is OK with remote ramp for 4-8 weeks for non-prod work. can she do code reviews and mentoring remotely pre-payroll?
ashley: yes, read-only repo access and meetings are fine. no write access or prod creds until payroll + bg check clear. we'll create a "remote-limited" access ticket.
marta: ok i'm comfortable with remote-limited. is relocation holdback policy triggered if start shifts?
ashley: policy: relocation reimbursement triggered by proof of physical relocation or first payroll check. we can approve a partial advance for moving expenses with finance sign-off. we'll route a relocation-advance form if needed.
kevin: action items from legal:
- Marta: share transfer receipt and passport page to secure portal and confirm intended stamping country
- Counsel (Kevin): confirm consulate appointment availability options and risk notes within 5 business days
- People-ops (Ashley): draft remote-limited onboarding list and coordinate relocation advance path with finance
- Comp/Finance: advise on whether sign-on advance is acceptable and tax setup
comp-bot: FYI: if we pay sign-on in advance while Marta is outside US, payroll will withhold based on US tax rules and may require additional forms (W-8/W-9 review).
nick: thanks everyone. please copy me on compensation/finance replies.
marta: uploading transfer receipt now. thanks for the flexibility.
ashley: opening HRIS ticket and setting hire_state = "pending_consular_stamping". will DM the remote checklist and relocation-advance form. expect email with next steps by EOD tomorrow.
kevin: I'll post a short memo on consular timing and risks in this thread within 3bd.
comp-bot: recorded provisional state = "pending_work_auth". no payroll or benefits enrollment until I-9 clears.
nick: closing loop for now. ping me for any blockers. :wave:
